newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - ABB holds Australia barley pool prices steady.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - ABB holds Australia barley pool prices steady.

text.p: The Australian Barley Board (ABB) has held its gross pool return estimates steady for Victorian and South Australian barley.
The pool price for Victorian malting barley was held at A$210.00 a tonne while the price for Victorian feed barley is steady at A$147.00 a tonne.
Estimated pools prices for South Australian barley have been held at A$210.00 a tonne for malting barley and A$142.00 a tonne for feed barley.
The board markets the barley grown in both states.
ABB chairman Ken Dingwall said it was extremely rare for ABB pools not to out-perform the average of cash prices over a season.
ABB also announced first advance payments for the season's barley pools.
Pool return estimates represent the ABB's current view of the barley market.
First advance payments are as high a proportion of the estimated gross return as can be achieved under the board's financing arrangements, Dingwall said.

The first payments ranged from A$110 a tonne for Feed Three barley in South Australia with an estimated residual of A$20-25 a tonne to A$180 for Franklin Malt One in both states with an estimated A$35-40 a tonne residual, the board said.
